business_scope.primary_industry_name: Stevedoring and Loading/Unloading of Bulk Cargo at Marine Docks

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Egypt (national territory; includes Egyptian port governorates and the Suez Canal Economic Zone relevant to the bulk port stevedoring terminal scope)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified Napoleonic-derived tradition; Islamic Sharia is the principal source of legislation under Article 2 of the 2014 Constitution)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: U.S.-Egypt Bilateral Investment Treaty (entered into force 27 June 1992)
Egypt-People's Republic of China Bilateral Investment Treaty (1994)
United Kingdom-Egypt Agreement for the Promotion and Protection of Investments (1975/1976)
EU-Egypt Association Agreement (2004) and the EU-Egypt investment protection framework
Unified Agreement for the Investment of Arab Capital in the Arab States (1980, as amended)
Agadir Agreement (2004) and COMESA Treaty rights (Egypt as member state)
Egypt's double taxation avoidance agreement network (e.g., UK, Germany, Kuwait, China)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Governance hierarchy: (i) Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended) governing LLC formation, memorandum of association, shareholder and manager disclosure obligations; (ii) Commercial Registration Law No. 34 of 1976 (as amended) mandating registration in the unified Commercial Registry (Shehrah); (iii) Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 2310 of 2017) establishing GAFI one-stop-shop incorporation, name clearance, UBO annexes and investment guarantees; (iv) Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002 (as amended by, inter alia, Law No. 78 of 2003 and Law No. 8 of 2015) and its Executive Regulations covering customer due diligence, UBO identification, record-keeping and suspicious transaction reporting; (v) Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194 of 2020 establishing and empowering the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU) as the national FIU; (vi) Egyptian Maritime Trade Law No. 8 of 1990 (as amended) and port authority regulations governing stevedoring and cargo-handling licensing; (vii) Egypt is not a contracting state to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; foreign documents require notarization, authentication and consular legalization by the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the competent Egyptian diplomatic mission.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of each non-Egyptian corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry or corporate registrar in the shareholder's country of registration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (notarization in origin country, authentication by competent authority, then legalization by the Egyptian diplomatic mission)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association (certified true copy) of the foreign parent shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or duly licensed notary in the origin jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution of the foreign shareholder authorizing incorporation of the Egyptian LLC, appointment of managers and designation of authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company secretary or notary of the foreign parent company

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport pages of each ultimate beneficial owner, proposed manager and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent civil registry in the UBO country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank credit reference or introduction letter for the founding shareholder(s)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank in the shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (Arabic and English) appointing the Egyptian incorporation counsel and registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Egyptian Notary Public Authority for in-country execution or foreign notary followed by consular legalization

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended), Articles 85-104 (LLC formation, quotas, management structure) and Article 1 (quota nominal value); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, Article 46 and Executive Regulations No. 2310 of 2017 (GAFI One-Stop-Shop, deemed approval, issuance of incorporation certificate); Law No. 5 of 2015 on Simplified Commercial Licensing (fee and procedural consolidation).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Companies Registration Department, One-Stop-Shop (al-Shubbak al-Wahid); Commercial Registry Office under GAFI supervision; for terminals inside the Suez Canal Economic Zone (e.g., Sokhna or Port Said East), the SCZone Investor Services Center may act as the single licensing window.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application (Namerou Qayd) supported by the executed and notarized Arabic-language Memorandum of Association (Contract of Incorporation) submitted via the GAFI One-Stop-Shop electronic portal and physical docket.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum aggregate paid-up capital for an LLC; however, the nominal value of each quota must be at least EGP 100. Cash contributions must be paid into a temporary corporate bank account at a bank licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt, and the bank's capital deposit certificate must accompany the GAFI filing; the deposited funds remain blocked until issuance of the incorporation certificate. In-kind contributions require a sworn valuation report by an accredited Egyptian accounting office.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION

The undersigned founders, as shareholders and initial managers of [Company Name] L.L.C. (the "Company"), a limited liability company in formation, resolve:

(1) That the Company's share capital, as set out in the executed Memorandum of Association, is fully subscribed and accepted.

(2) That the registered head office be established at [Address], Alexandria/Port Said, Egypt, for service of statutory notices and corporate records.

(3) That [Name] is appointed Managing Director and legal representative, and [Name] is appointed Secretary/Compliance Officer, each authorized to register the Company and complete all licensing steps, including stevedoring licenses, before GAFI and the Maritime Transport Sector.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Trade Name Registration Unit via e-GAFI online portal (www.gafi.gov.eg) or GAFI One-Stop-Shop front desk.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online application listing three alternative trade names in descending preference. GAFI screens against the Commercial Registry index for identical or deceptively similar names and against protected trademarks. Upon clearance, GAFI issues a provisional name reservation certificate valid for six months, which must be attached to the incorporation contract.
required_dossiers: GAFI trade name reservation application form
Copies of founding shareholders' national IDs (Egyptian) or passports (non-residents)
Legalized power of attorney if foreign founders act through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, the legal representative may file a written reconsideration request with the GAFI Name Screening Committee within 30 days, and simultaneously submit up to three fresh alternative names for re-screening without additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Memorandum of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Notary Public (Maa'muriyat al-Shahr al-'Aqari) at the competent notary office; for foreign founders, translation by a translator accredited by the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founders or their authorized representatives appear before the notary to execute the Arabic-language Memorandum of Association. The notary verifies identity and legal capacity, records the notarial minutes, stamps the contract, and returns certified copies for subsequent GAFI filing.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum of Association in Arabic
Proof of registered office (lease agreement or ownership title deed)
Legalized/authenticated power of attorney for foreign founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues a reasoned refusal, the founders may correct the documented deficiencies and re-submit to the same notary, or file a petition with the head of the notary office; extreme cases may be resolved by a court order from the competent economic court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any commercial bank licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt (corporate account opening desk).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate bank account in the company's name using the draft or notarized MoA, deposit the founders' cash capital contributions, and obtain the bank's capital deposit certificate confirming the amount and account details in the company's name. The account remains blocked until the GAFI incorporation certificate is presented.
required_dossiers: Notarized or draft Memorandum of Association
Identification documents of the account signatories
Statement of capital allocation among shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises KYC deficiencies, the legal representative remedies the requests within 10 business days or selects an alternative CBE-licensed bank; a fresh deposit certificate is issued on completion of the account opening.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI One-Stop-Shop Incorporation Filing and Certificate Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop-Shop (GAFI branch competent for the registered office; SCZone Investor Services Center for terminals inside the Suez Canal Economic Zone).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized incorporation package and the electronic company registration form through the One-Stop-Shop. Pay the consolidated statutory fees to the treasury. The One-Stop-Shop issues the Company's Certificate of Incorporation (Shahadat Qayd al-Sharika), activates the initial Commercial Registry entry, and transmits the file to the tax and social insurance authorities; a deemed approval applies if no objection is raised within the statutory review window.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum of Association (two certified copies)
First Board Resolution (appointment of managers and registered office approval)
Lease contract for the registered office
Identity documents or passports, with legalized translations for foreign founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a justified deficiency note, the founders cure the defects within 15 days without re-payment of fees. Silence or delay beyond 4 working days after submission leads to deemed approval of the registration under the Investment Law's deemed-approval principle; rejections may be appealed to the GAFI Dispute Settlement Committee within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), integrated window at the GAFI One-Stop-Shop, and the local tax office competent for the registered office address.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The GAFI incorporation transmission automatically allocates a provisional tax number and generates the tax registration file. The company completes the ETA file by submitting physical copies of the lease, the MoA, and directors' ID documents, and receives the final Tax Card (al-Bataqa al-Daribiyya) covering income tax and VAT registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax card is not issued within five working days through the One-Stop-Shop, the company applies directly to the competent local tax office using the GAFI receipt; corrections to the registration data are submitted by amended application; inter-agency delays are escalated to the GAFI service manager for expedited clearance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social Insurance Registration and Post-Registration Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI) - employer registration bureau transmitted through the GAFI One-Stop-Shop; engraving of company seal through an authorized government-audited engraver.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: GAFI forwards the establishment data to NOSI, which issues the employer insurance file number (Form 1 - Bayan al-Munsha'a) and enrolls the founding managers. The company engraves its corporate seal, obtains specimen signatures, and opens the final operational bank account by presenting the incorporation certificate and board resolution.
required_dossiers: Board resolution specifying bank signing mandates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NOSI queries the submitted data, the employer files corrected forms within two weeks; penalties for late registration are waived when registration is completed within the first 30 days of incorporation; unresolved disputes are referred to the NOSI internal appeal committee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Maritime Transport Sector (MTS), Ministry of Transport, together with the cargo handling licensing department of the competent Egyptian Port Authority (Alexandria Port Authority, Damietta Port Authority, or General Authority of Red Sea Ports); for terminals inside the Suez Canal Economic Zone (Port Said East or Sokhna), the SCZone Ports and Terminals Department issues the concession and operating approvals.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: License to Practice Cargo Handling (Stevedoring) Operations at Maritime Ports and Terminal Operating Concession (Berth/Quay Use and Storage Yard Allocation) issued under Law No. 1 of 1996 on the Organization of Maritime Ports (as amended) and Law No. 12 of 1996 on Maritime Commerce, with the stevedoring contract concluded through the Port Authority's licensed stevedores registry.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) - Environmental Licensing Department, coordinated with the Port Authority's Environmental Compliance Unit and, within SCZone, the SCZone Environment, Health and Safety Department.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Initial Environmental Scoping with Full Environmental Impact Assessment Report (Form B) required under Law No. 4 of 1994 (as amended by Law No. 9 of 2009). Bulk cargo stevedoring terminals with particulate emission potential, cargo storage yards, and marine discharge points are classified as a listed activity requiring an EIA prepared by an EEAA-accredited environmental consultant and approved by EEAA prior to terminal operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Law No. 4 of 1994 and Ministerial Decree No. 402 of 2009 (effluent discharge into marine waters): oil and grease not exceeding 15 mg/L, total suspended solids not exceeding 60 mg/L, BOD5 not exceeding 60 mg/L, and COD not exceeding 100 mg/L; ambient air quality for PM10 not exceeding 150 µg/m3 (24-hour mean) with dust suppression at conveyors, hoppers, and storage piles; compliance with IMO MARPOL Annexes I-V for ship-generated waste, oily water, and ballast water management per the Ballast Water Management Convention; spill prevention, containment, and response plan for bulk cargo residues.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Fire Safety Certificate from the General Administration of Civil Defense (Ministry of Interior) covering terminal sheds, conveyor galleries, hopper structures, and any fuel storage, including fire suppression systems, hydrant coverage, and emergency egress; structural load and quay wall safety clearance issued by the Port Authority Engineering Directorate for crane foundations, mooring bollards, and conveyor support frames; occupational safety and workplace clearance under Labor Law No. 12 of 2003 and Ministerial Decree No. 211 of 2003, covering crane operator certification, personal protective equipment, terminal traffic management, first-aid stations, and the port health certificate for sanitation and potable water in terminal buildings.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — official national tax administration; electronic portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign investor incorporated as an Egyptian LLC must first complete commercial registration with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) or the Ministry of Trade and Industry, obtain the commercial registration certificate and national ID data, then apply to the Egyptian Tax Authority for a Tax Identification Number (TIN) through the ETA portal or a certified tax accountant. The application requires the certificate of incorporation, memorandum of association, commercial registration, legal representation documents, proof of registered address, and national ID/passport copies of directors and shareholders. The TIN is issued free of charge and serves as the VAT registration number where VAT registration is triggered.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election and no hybrid mismatch election mechanism exists under Egyptian tax law for an LLC. Classification as a separate taxable legal entity is mandatory and determined by the company’s commercial registration under the Companies Law and the Corporate Income Tax regime administered by the Egyptian Tax Authority.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Egypt operates a mandatory e-invoicing and e-receipt system administered by the Egyptian Tax Authority. Taxable persons, including stevedoring operators at ports, must integrate their billing systems with the ETA’s certified electronic invoice platform via API, transmit invoice data in real time for fiscal clearance, and print invoices bearing a digital stamp/QR code approved by the ETA. Non-compliance leads to rejection of invoices for tax credit and applicable penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to exports of goods physically delivered or shipped outside Egypt, to international transportation services, and to certain services rendered to non-resident parties that are not consumed within Egypt. Port stevedoring services for export-bound bulk cargo are zero-rated where the service is directly connected to and substantiated as an export transaction. The taxpayer must hold adequate commercial and customs evidence demonstrating the goods have left Egyptian customs territory and been delivered into an export destination.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bayan) stamped by Egyptian Customs
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Sea Waybill evidencing export shipment from the port terminal
Inward Remittance Certificate / foreign currency receipt evidencing payment of consideration from abroad
Validated stevedoring service invoice contract identifying the exporter, cargo, port, vessel, and destination
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Egyptian Tax Authority actively audits zero-rated export claims, focusing on the completeness of customs departure evidence, the direct link between stevedoring services and an actual export cargo movement, and timely repatriation of foreign currency. If documentation is incomplete, fraudulent, or repatriation deadlines are breached, the ETA may reverse the zero rating and assess VAT at the standard rate, add statutory late interest/penalty surcharges, and impose monetary fines under the VAT Law. Criminal sanctions, including imprisonment and enhanced penalties, may apply where fraudulent invoicing or deliberate evasion is established with intent.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Egyptian Pound is partially convertible: current-account transactions are liberalized, while capital-account movements (portfolio investment, shareholder loans, and foreign direct investment repatriation) are subject to CBE registration and approval. Profit remittance from a stevedoring LLC is permitted if the following are submitted to the CBE-licensed corporate bank: (a) audited financial statements, (b) tax clearance certificate, (c) GAFI investment registration, and (d) proof that the EGP funds were obtained through CBE-approved conversion or an FX account. In practice, USD availability for dividends may be constrained during BoP stress, though the March 2024 exchange-rate unification removed mandatory surrender requirements and allows banks to fund outflows from market purchases.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For bulk-port cargo-handling services (ISIC 5224), export proceeds in foreign currency must be received in a CBE-licensed Egyptian bank account within 180 days from the service completion date or bill-of-lading date, whichever is later. There is no mandatory conversion ratio under the current unified/flexible exchange-rate regime; however, the exporter must offer the proceeds to a bank for conversion EGP at the interbank rate unless the proceeds are held in a foreign-currency account with a licensed Egyptian bank. Failure to repatriate within the stated period may trigger CBE penalties, suspension of import licences, and blocked banking facilities.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore fintech/EMI (electronic money institution) cannot directly open onshore corporate accounts or access the Egyptian clearing system without obtaining a CBE licence under the new Banking Law (Law No. 194 of 2020). Such institutions may be used only for non-set-off, preparatory global collections, but all EGP settlement must pass through a CBE-licensed payment service provider or a commercial bank. For a stevedoring terminal, a pure offshore EMI is operationally unsuitable for local port-authority clearing, customs payments, or EGP working-capital management.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory. CBE requires the ultimate beneficial owner, the general manager, and two authorized signatories to attend a face-to-face KYB interview at the chosen bank branch. For foreign-owned LLCs, a distant-learnt remote interview may be accepted only if accompanied by a notarized and apostilled power of attorney, a certified board resolution, and a pre-registered electronic signature. In practice, banks in Egypt reject remote-only opening for capital-intensive terminal operators and demand original statutory documents (incorporation certificates, tax card, GAFI licence, port authority concession).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Heavy cash-intensive port-authority, stevedoring, and freight settlements that appear inconsistent with operating activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commissioned operational agreement, port authority tariff schedule, inward cargo manifest, contract with the bulk cargo owners, and a monthly reconciliation between berth receipts and bank credits; an accounting policy note confirming all sales to port users are invoice-based and settled by bank transfer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO resides in or funds originate from high-risk/jurisdiction sanction-listed entities transacting through maritime corridors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanction-screening records of counterparties (vessel owners, cargo shippers, charterers), Politically Exposed Persons declaration, approved list of approved trade partners from the bank, and a compliance undertaking to suspend cargo operations if sanctions are triggered.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign currency inflow arrives from a third-country beneficiary unrelated to a known trading contract.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Charter party and bill-of-lading copies, the original SWIFT MT103 / MT202 message, the export invoice, customs export declaration, and a written explanation signed by the CFO stating the commercial basis. All hedging instruments must be linked to an underlying real trade exposure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign shareholders should transmit the equity injection via SWIFT MT103 from the originating bank to the entity's CBE-licensed corporate account at the Tier-1 Egyptian bank, using the standard remittance narrative 'Equity contribution for EG_LLC'. The receiving bank must issue an inward transfer voucher (MT910) and complete a CBE-based purpose code 'Capital Investment – Direct Equity'. For a stevedoring LLC, the capital must be registered with the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) and the CBE capital-inflow database within one month of receipt to permit future profit repatriation; funds can be held in USD or converted to EGP at the interbank rate. No government approval is required for the capital injection itself, but the account must be pre-opened and the bank's AML review cleared before funds arrive.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound operating payments (port fees, equipment leases, subcontracted stevedoring services, and international suppliers) should be executed via (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct invoices, with a CBE purpose code matching the service category; (ii) commercial letters of credit (L/C at sight or 30-60 days) for procurement of port machinery, computer systems, or major capital equipment; and (iii) central bank-regulated direct debit mechanisms for domestic Egyptian tax payments and port authority settlements. Profit repatriation and dividend distribution must be routed through the same Tier-1 bank that manages the capital account after submission of audited financial statements, a tax clearance certificate (accepted within 10 business days), and a CBE dividend-remittance approval. A separate escrow may be required for remittances exceeding USD 100,000 equivalent until the underlying trade invoices are verified.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable forward FX contracts (USD/EGP) with licensed Egyptian banks for up to 12 months, subject to underlying trade/hedging documentation
FX swaps for trade-related operational cash-flow mitigation (repetitive purchase and sale of EGP vs USD between the corporate and the banking counterparty)
Cross-currency swaps for medium-term infrastructure debt (e.g., a USD-EGP interest-rate/principal exchange on port-equipment financing or bank loans)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registry Renewal (Commercial Registration Certificate) under Law 34/1976
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office, Ministry of Trade and Industry (filed via the GAFI electronic registration platform)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary month of the company's original registration; renewal accepted from 30 days before up to 60 days after the registration anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delay fee of EGP 200–2,000 escalating monthly; after 60 days the registry record is flagged inactive; prolonged non-renewal triggers administrative strike-off, loss of legal capacity, and blocking of bank accounts and Port Authority transactions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Tax Card Renewal (Tax Identity Card) under Law 9/1960 and Law 91/2005
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – local Tax Office of the company's registered jurisdiction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Before the expiry date on the existing tax card (anniversary of issuance); renewal application submitted during the final month of card validity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-renewal fine of EGP 1,000–2,000; an expired tax card invalidates customs releases, port gate access, and stevedoring clearances at Egyptian seaports; continued unlicensed activity exposes managers to criminal fines

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 42) accompanied by audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Large or Mid-size Taxpayer Unit, or local tax office depending on registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 April following the end of the tax year (Egyptian corporate tax year default: calendar year, 1 January – 31 December)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-payment surcharge of 2% of unpaid assessed corporate tax; non-filing fixed fine of EGP 500–20,000 plus delay interest at Central Bank discount rate + 2% per annum; persistent default results in tax liens against bank accounts and port receivables, not administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Confirmation and Update of the Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – UBO electronic register; notices to the Egyptian Money Laundering Combating Unit (EMLCU) where discrepancies arise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation filed concurrently with the Commercial Registry renewal; mandatory update within 15 days of any share transfer, change of control, or change in beneficial ownership (reporting threshold: direct or indirect holding of 10% or more, or de facto control)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of EGP 20,000 to EGP 1,000,000 for failure to file or material omission of UBO data (AML Law 80/2002, amended by Law 115/2017); incorrect register entries may void shareholder resolutions and attract EMLCU sanctions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Social Insurance Wage Declaration and insured-persons statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the end of February of the year following the reporting period; monthly contribution forms remain separately due by the 15th of each following month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 2% monthly late-contribution charge on unpaid premiums; under-declaration of stevedoring wages is a criminal offense for LLC managers; lapse of the NOSI registration certificate blocks bank payroll processing and port labor permits

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit is compulsory for every Egyptian LLC without a size or turnover exemption: Law 159/1981 (as amended) requires the appointment of at least one auditor registered with the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA); the audited financial statements must accompany the annual corporate income tax return filed with ETA
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) issued by the FRA and converged with IFRS; the stevedoring LLC applies EAS 1 (presentation of financial statements), EAS 28 (revenue), EAS 13 (inventories), EAS 25 (property, plant and equipment), and the port concession operating rights are accounted under EAS standards aligned with IFRS 16 / IFRIC 12 principles

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Egypt imposes a mandatory UBO register regime: the LLC must record every beneficial owner (individuals holding or controlling more than 10% directly or indirectly, or exercising de facto control) and confirm this data annually with GAFI at the time of the Commercial Registry renewal; any share transfer or change of control must be reflected in the UBO register within 15 days through a board resolution and updated filing; the external auditor verifies UBO consistency with the register of members during the annual audit and reports material discrepancies to the EMLCU
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members and shareholding transfers (Shareholders' Register)
Register of Managers/Directors with specimen signatures and resolutions
Minute Book of General Assemblies and Management Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 – 1,000 per annum (registered office lease attestation, company secretarial support, mail handling and statutory filing follow-up in Cairo or Alexandria)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 – 6,000 per annum (FRA-licensed audit firm conducting a full statutory audit of an active stevedoring LLC with port receivables, vessel services and fixed assets)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25.0% marginal rate on taxable corporate income exceeding EGP 40,000 under Law No. 2 of 2023 (integrated progressive schedule: 10% up to EGP 5,000; 15% on EGP 5,001-20,000; 22.5% on EGP 20,001-40,000; 25% above EGP 40,000)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Investment Law No. 72 of 2017: 50% deduction of investment costs for 7 years or 50% tax holiday for 5 years for qualifying terminal infrastructure; Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) projects may access up to 5 years of 0% corporate tax followed by a 50% reduction for an additional 5 years; statutory depreciation and 5-year loss carryforward reductions lower the effective terminal rate to approximately 18-22.5% before zone incentives

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return Form No. 3 ('Iqrar'; Arabic and English versions available); mandatory electronic filing through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) national e-tax portal at www.eta.gov.eg
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return, complemented by mandatory quarterly advance instalment declarations (ETA instalment forms due shortly after the 3rd, 6th, 9th month for large-port operators with recurring stevedoring revenue)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return and final tax payment must be filed no later than four calendar months after the fiscal year-end; fiscal year aligned to the calendar year unless a different accounting period is pre-approved by the ETA

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross stevedoring receipts: total bulk-cargo loading/discharging tariffs, whatrage, demurrage and ancillary dock service revenue in EGP
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an EG LLC owned by non-residents, include 100% of Egypt-source gross revenue; non-resident foreign-flagged operators without an Egyptian PE report only Egypt-source stevedoring income and may claim treaty maritime/navigation protections where applicable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct operating costs: stevedore wages, fuel, terminal equipment repairs, berth-rent and port authority levies
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach port-authority statements, payroll registers and certified sub-contractor invoices to substantiate deductions; the ETA will disallow undocumented cash labour costs in non-resident-controlled terminals

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital allowances and depreciation on cranes, conveyors, barges and terminal buildings per Executive Regulation depreciation schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If barges and cranes are leased from a foreign related party, the lease/royalty element is separately subject to 20% WHT unless a treaty reduction is pre-approved; depreciation on assets not paid into Egypt is not deductible

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after claiming the 5-year tax loss carryforward, Investment Law incentives, and disallowed expense add-backs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders: attach the ETA incentive approval reference and ensure any treaty-based position is declared by a contemporaneous transfer pricing form if related-party expenses exceed EGP 10,000,000

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate tax computed under the Law 2/2023 progressive brackets (10%, 15%, 22.5%, 25%)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax on the stevedoring LLC is assessed at entity level; non-resident shareholders cannot offset personal tax on the LLC's income; impose and declare dividend WHT in the shareholders' distribution schedule

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of quarterly advance tax instalments and foreign tax credits against the gross annual corporate tax assessed
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are allowed only with a certified foreign tax assessment demonstrating economic double taxation; ETA may require a TRC if treaty relief is also claimed on the same profit

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of dividends resolved or repatriated to non-resident shareholders: withholding tax computation at 10% and any treaty-reduced rate applied
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete DTA relief annex, attach the apostilled Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership declaration; without prior ETA clearance the LLC must withhold the statutory 10% and the shareholder files a refund claim within five years

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 2% monthly surcharge on the tax due, capped at 8%; late payment: 1.5% monthly charge up to 30% per Law No. 173/2020; inaccurate or materially incomplete returns: additional 40% of the understated tax; failure to e-file on the ETA portal: administrative fines of up to EGP 50,000 plus escalation to criminal sanctions for non-filing beyond 6 months

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty-reduced dividend rates, the non-resident shareholder must (a) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate in the treaty jurisdiction for the calendar year of distribution, apostilled/legalised and certified-translated into Arabic; (b) file the ETA treaty-relief form, together with the TRC, shareholding certificate, audited financial statements and a beneficial ownership declaration, with the ETA International Taxation Unit before the date of distribution; (c) if no advance clearance is obtained, the Egyptian LLC must withhold the full statutory 10%, and the shareholder must apply to ETA for a refund within five years from the end of the year of payment; (d) ETA will deny relief if the foreign shareholder lacks economic substance or is interposed primarily to secure treaty benefits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and technical/management fees: statutory 20% domestic WHT; treaty caps commonly 10% (e.g., Egypt-UAE, Egypt-Netherlands) to 12.5% (e.g., Egypt-UK). Interest on cross-border loans from non-resident lenders: statutory 20% WHT; treaty caps normally 10%-15%, with several DTAs (e.g., Egypt-UK) reducing interest to 10%; interest payments to related parties also require transfer pricing verification. Egypt-source rules follow either payer-residence in Egypt or the economic use of the royalty/loan within Egypt.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: mandatory when Egyptian controlled transactions exceed the documented ETA threshold of EGP 10,000,000 per year (ETA Decision No. 477/2021). Master File: mandatory when the Egyptian stevedoring entity's annual revenue exceeds EGP 200,000,000 or the consolidated worldwide group revenue exceeds EGP 4,000,000,000. Country-by-Country Report: aligned to the EGP 4,000,000,000 group-revenue threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not operate a standalone GCC-style Economic Substance Regulations filing regime; nevertheless, the Egyptian Tax Authority applies the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (Income Tax Law No. 91/2005, Article 89), the place-of-effective-management test, and anti-conduit jurisprudence to attack shell structures. For a licensed bulk-port stevedoring terminal, substantive requirements include: dedicated berth and terminal agreements, operating cranes and conveyors physically located in Egypt, licensed stevedore labour payroll, port-authority attendance logs, and board decisions taken in Egyptian territory. Absence of these indicia will trigger GAAR recharacterisation of the LLC as an agency of the foreign parent and impose full Egyptian tax on agency profits, disallowance of related-party deductions, and a 10% deemed dividend WHT.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration or non-filing of bulk stevedoring revenue; collection of cash tariffs from shipowners without issuing ETA-approved e-invoices; destruction of berth-service logs; falsification of vessel discharge manifests to reduce taxable turnover
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine equal to twice the entire evaded tax; imprisonment for 3 to 5 years under Article 133 of Law No. 91/2005 as amended by Law No. 173/2020; judicial settlement permitted only before criminal referral; additional monthly 1.5% late-payment surcharge up to 30% on the unpaid balance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general managers prosecution in criminal capacity; personal restitution orders for evaded tax; passport seizure and travel bans imposed by ETA enforcement; disqualification from corporate directorship for up to five years upon conviction

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misstatement and Undocumented Related-Party Charges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying a foreign parent inflated 'stevedoring management fees', 'demurrage software charges' or 'vessel coordination fees' without an approved TP study; failing to file Local File when controlled transactions exceed EGP 10,000,000; failure to submit Master File notwithstanding the EGP 200,000,000 revenue threshold
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA transfer pricing adjustment recharacterising excess charges as sham expenses; additional tax at the 25% bracket on the adjusted amount; 40% penalty on the tax under-declared; documentation penalties of up to EGP 50,000 per missing file; interest and delay surcharges compounding
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: CFO and signatories of the corporate tax return become jointly liable for the corrected tax where knowingly mismanaged; personal fines equal to the penalty cap; administrative attachment of personal bank accounts and travel restrictions pending settlement

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Economic Substance Abuse under GAAR (Article 89, Law 91/2005)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing the EG LLC solely to hold berth concession contracts while operational decisions, employees, and cranes remain owned by the foreign parent; stripping Egypt-source stevedoring profit to a zero-tax offshore entity via nominee service agreements; absence of physical terminal office and marine equipment registry in Egypt
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA disregards the LLC separating scenario; total recharacterisation of the non-resident parent as having a permanent establishment in Egypt; denial of all inflated service deductions; payment of 25% tax on deemed Egyptian profit plus 10% deemed dividend WHT on repatriation; anti-abuse penalty of 200% of under-assessed tax in flagsaving cases
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Beneficial owners and nominees face personal liability for tax and penalties to the extent of distributions received; veil-piercing orders issued by the Economic Courts; international travel bans; in aggravated instances, imprisonment for up to 3 years for submitting false sworn declarations

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Trade-Based Money Laundering and Sanctions Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using stevedoring invoices to over- or under-invoice bulk cargo values; handling cargo consigned to sanctioned entities or from prohibited jurisdictions; receiving stevedoring fees through unlicensed currency brokers or uncleared cash intermediaries; failing to file suspicious transaction reports with the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to EGP 500,000 and forfeiture of proceeds under Law No. 80 of 2002 as amended; imprisonment up to 15 years for laundering predicates; additional suspension of port-terminal licence by the port authority; asset seizure orders enforceable against the LLC and its bank accounts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: AML compliance directors incur personal criminal liability for failure to report suspicious bulk-cargo payment patterns; personal passport surrender and blanket travel bans imposed during investigation; personal and family assets subject to seizure; permanent managerial debarment from Egyptian port concessions upon conviction
